conviction_note: Near-balanced: a crowded and rising short (27.3% of float, 6 days to cover) into a stock down 32% since the last print, with the sell side already cutting FY numbers below the company guide, offsets real cost and demand headwinds (HRC steel +52% y/y, housing turnover at the year's low, mortgage rates rising); p_up 53 on a 13% absolute move gives +0.78, close to the +0.7 findings sum, and both are small because the guide cut is expected and the size of the cut is the unknown.
bar: Q3 2026 ongoing EPS consensus disputed: $0.93 on $3.96bn revenue (MarketBeat, 2026-10-19, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-whirlpool-whr-projected-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/) vs $1.01 from 8 analysts (AAII, 2026-10-26, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/525369-what-you-need-to-know-about-whirlpool-corporations-q3-earnings); the sweep's $0.78 is unsourced. Q3 2025 was $2.09 EPS on $4.03bn including India, which has since been deconsolidated. The FY bar matters more: company guide ongoing EPS $2.50-3.00, revenue ~$15.0bn, ongoing EBIT margin ~4%, FCF >$300m, net debt <$5.0bn (Q2 release, 2026-08-03, https://whirlpool.mediaroom.com/2026-08-03-Whirlpool-Corporation-Announces-Second-Quarter-Results). Street FY sits below the guide: MarketBeat $2.25; AAII says current-year estimates fell 14.8% in a month and puts the forward P/E at 14.7, about $1.80 at today's price. H1 ongoing EPS was -$0.56 + -$0.21 = -$0.77, so the guide implies H2 of $3.27-3.77. The Q3 bar comes from two disagreeing sources, so findings on the reported quarter are capped small.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest at 2026-09-30 (published 2026-10-09): 17,465,715 shares, 27.3% of float, 5.96 days to cover, up 12.4% from 15.53m on 09-15 and up from 13.7m on 07-31; it has risen on every settlement since mid-July (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/WHR/short-interest/ ; equibles gives the same FINRA rows and models ~17.8m for 10-15, https://equibles.com/stocks/whr/shortinterest). Skew_25d +0.86 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.98, event-implied move 12.21%, straddle 16.93%. Tape: spot 26.58, -15.4% over 20 days, -71% from the 52-week high, 0.4% above the 52-week low. Millennium filed a 13G for 5.3% (event 2026-10-13), likely a hedged or market-neutral book. A crowded short: the squeeze is a real mechanism and every negative below is shrunk for it.

findings.finding: The FY guide will almost certainly be cut, and the street has already cut ahead of it. The $2.50-3.00 ongoing EPS guide (2026-08-03) implies H2 EPS of $3.27-3.77 after H1's -$0.77. Street FY is $2.25 (MarketBeat) to about $1.80 (AAII: forward P/E 14.7, estimates -14.8% in a month). In the week before the print Longbow, the bull who asked the first question on the Q2 call, went Buy to Neutral on 2026-10-19, citing H2 burdens 'not adequately reflected' in the company guide. Citi ($48 to $32), Goldman ($48 to $41), RBC ($32 to $22, Underperform), Wells Fargo ($39 to $30) and BofA ($38 to $31) all cut targets between September and October. The bar has been reset low; what is unknown is whether the new guide lands above or below roughly $1.80-2.25.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (2026-05-06): guide cut from ~$7 to $3.00-3.50 and dividend suspended, -11.91%. Q2 2026 (2026-08-03): guide cut to $2.50-3.00 on interest expense and an EPS miss vs consensus, +13.80%, a relief rally with short interest above 21%. July 2025: guide and dividend cut, -13.43%.
findings.why_not_priced: A cut to roughly $2.00 is in the price: the stock is -32% since 08-03, estimates have been cut and targets sit at $22-41. What is not priced is the size of the cut. If the market had priced a cut to $1.00-1.50 (steel, fuel and housing all moving against the H2 ramp), the stock would trade below RBC's $22. If it had priced the guide being held, it would not sit at the 52-week low with SI rising.
findings.independence: AAII revision data (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/525369-what-you-need-to-know-about-whirlpool-corporations-q3-earnings) and MarketBeat's analyst-action list (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-whirlpool-nyse-whr-shares-gap-up-should-you-buy-2026-10-20/) are separate sources for the same estimate reset. The guide arithmetic rests on the company's Q2 release.

findings.finding: US hot-rolled coil hit $1,220-1,300/short ton on 2026-10-16, against $825-865 a year earlier (+52% y/y and a four-year high), and Nucor kept raising its CSP every week from $1,190 on 09-08. On the Q2 call (2026-08-04) the CEO said Whirlpool was already 'on the very high end of the contracts' on steel and that raw materials cost 50bp of margin in Q2, with resin pressure on top. This bears on the Q4 and 2027 cost framing rather than the reported quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raw-material and tariff cost commentary was part of the Q1 2026 cut (-11.91%) and the July 2025 cut (-13.43%). On its own the line has never been isolated in a reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Steel is a public series, so part of this is in the stock. What has not been seen is Whirlpool's own number for the H2 and 2027 raw-material headwind. If it were priced, consensus FY would already carry a quantified steel line; the visible cuts are framed around demand and interest.
findings.independence: Q2 transcript, company's own steel comment (https://s202.q4cdn.com/229739679/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/WHR-US-CORRECTED-TRANSCRIPT-Whirlpool-CorpWHRUS-Q2-2026-Earnings-Call-4August2026-800-ET-AM-03-08-2026-2026-08-03-0.pdf). This is a proxy: Whirlpool's contract timing is unknown.

findings.finding: An independent pricing series supports Q3 price realisation. OpenBrand's appliance discount frequency fell from 41.5% (June) to 40.8% (July), 38.3% (August, revised) and 35.7% (September), and appliance prices rose m/m in each month (+0.14%, +0.24%, +0.09%). The independent price data therefore supports management's Q2-call claim that Q3 gets the full promo-price increase (only two-thirds of it landed in Q2), plus a ~4% July list increase and builder price increases. That is the basis on which the CEO said he expects a Q3 North America margin step-up similar to Q1-to-Q2 (+240bp, implying NA around 5%+ from 2.7%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 delivered the promised sequential margin step (+50bp group, +240bp NA) and the stock rose 13.8% despite an EPS miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus of ~$0.93-1.01 already assumes an EBIT margin step to about 4%+ in Q3, so price realisation is partly in the bar. If the market believed it fully, the stock would not have fallen 32% while the discounting data improved month after month. Industry discounting falling to 35.7% is not a figure any preview quoted.
findings.independence: OpenBrand August report (https://openbrand.com/newsroom/blog/cpi-august-2026) is the same series. Management's Q2-call guidance on the Q3 step-up (https://s202.q4cdn.com/229739679/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/WHR-US-CORRECTED-TRANSCRIPT-Whirlpool-CorpWHRUS-Q2-2026-Earnings-Call-4August2026-800-ET-AM-03-08-2026-2026-08-03-0.pdf) is a different source pointing the same way. Industry series, not a Whirlpool number; capped because the bar is disputed.

findings.finding: Q3 housing turnover and rates moved against volume. NAR (2026-10-13): September existing-home sales were 3.99m SAAR, -2.2% y/y, and August-September were the two slowest months of 2026. The Freddie Mac 30-year averaged 6.86% in September, against 6.67% in August and 6.35% a year earlier. US industry demand was already -3.4% y/y in Q2. Best Buy's large-appliance comp was only +0.2% in May-July, against a -9.2% prior-year base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Demand commentary ('recession-level industry decline', comparable to the GFC) drove the Q1 2026 reaction of -11.91%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: housing data is public and the stock fell 7.8% on 09-01 on housing and debt. What remains is how Whirlpool's Q4 industry assumption moves; a stated industry decline worse than -3% for H2 would be new.
findings.independence: Best Buy 10-Q appliance comp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000764478/000076447826000042/bby-20260801.htm) is a separate counterparty and flat-ish rather than negative. Macro proxy; Whirlpool has not confirmed Q3 volumes.

findings.finding: Crowded and building short into the print. FINRA SI was 17.47m shares (27.3% of float, 5.96 days to cover) at 2026-09-30, up from 13.7m at 07-31, and rose on every settlement since mid-July. The stock is -32% since the 08-03 print and 0.4% above its 52-week low. The last print, an EPS miss with an EPS-guide cut, produced +13.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-03: SI around 21-23% of float, a guide cut and EPS miss, +13.80%. 2025-10-27: +5.15%. Three of seven prints up.
findings.why_not_priced: SI is public, but the option market prices the move as balanced (skew +0.86, P/C OI 0.98). If a squeeze were priced, call skew would be bid. A 'less bad' guide on 27% SI with ~6 days to cover has a covering mechanism of its own.
findings.independence: Equibles carries the same FINRA settlement series (https://equibles.com/stocks/whr/shortinterest), so it is the same data and not independent.

findings.finding: Cash delivery is the second line after EPS. H1 free cash flow was -$1.1bn against a FY guide of >$300m, so H2 must generate about $1.4bn. Net debt was $5.8bn at Q2 against a year-end target below $5.0bn. On the Q2 call management said inventory entered H2 balanced, with no Q3-Q4 production correction needed. The 09-01 drop of 7.8% was attributed to the $7.1bn debt load. The financing itself (a $2bn ABL and $2bn secured notes) cleared maturities to 2028, so it is not the risk; Q3 FCF and any change to the FCF or net-debt targets are.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Debt and cash concerns drove the 2026-09-01 move (-7.8%) and the June secured-notes day (-5.8%); not isolated on a print day.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced through the drawdown. A cut to the FCF or net-debt target alongside a lower EBIT guide would be new; a held FCF guide would be read as a relief. The sign depends on the Q3 working-capital number, which nobody outside has.
findings.independence: Q2 transcript, inventory and cash commentary (https://s202.q4cdn.com/229739679/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/WHR-US-CORRECTED-TRANSCRIPT-Whirlpool-CorpWHRUS-Q2-2026-Earnings-Call-4August2026-800-ET-AM-03-08-2026-2026-08-03-0.pdf); ts2.tech on the 09-01 debt drop (https://ts2.tech/en/whirlpool-stock-falls-7-8-as-7-1-billion-debt-magnifies-housing-strain/).

findings.finding: SDA Global (KitchenAid, about $200m a quarter at ~12% EBIT margin) told the market a 'temporary but sizable trade inventory burn' in Q2 would correct in Q3, with US POS up 16% and global sell-through up high teens. A Q3 snapback is a small segment positive. Net of the rest of the company it is worth little: SDA is about 5% of sales against NA's ~68%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside what management guided, so mostly expected; filed small.

findings.finding: LG Electronics' Q3 2026 preliminary results (2026-10-07) showed revenue +8.9% and operating profit +13.5% y/y. Home appliances were named a key contributor, with cost improvements offsetting logistics and materials. A major US competitor's appliance business is growing while Whirlpool's sales fall, which hints at share pressure, though LG's growth is global.
findings.why_not_priced: Public peer print, but no US-specific split; Whirlpool claimed flat NA share YTD. This is a weak proxy.
findings.independence: Whirlpool's own Q2-call claim of flat share (transcript) points the other way.

findings.finding: Millennium Management filed a 13G on 2026-10-20 for 3,471,173 shares (5.3%), event date 2026-10-13, with zero sole voting power: a new passive 5% holder in the fortnight before the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Multi-manager books are often hedged, so the direction is unknown; sized at zero.

findings.finding: 8-K of 2026-10-20 (item 5.02): Karin Risi, a former Vanguard senior executive, was appointed to the board and to the Finance and HR committees, effective 10-19. A governance addition a week before the print, with no executive departure.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial to the print; filed for completeness.

baseline_tension: Balanced skew (+0.86) and a -15% 20-day run-up to the 52-week low, with a building 27% short. The negatives I found (steel, housing, the guide cut) are the same story the drawdown and the target cuts already tell, so they mostly agree with the price. The one thing that cuts against the price is positioning, which is why the net is slightly positive and small.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed: $0.93 vs $1.01, sweep $0.78 unsourced): the reported-quarter pricing finding was capped from +1.5 to +1.0
Rule 7 (crowded short, 27.3% of float, 6 DTC): every negative shrunk once: guide -1.0 to -0.7, steel -1.5 to -1.0, housing -1.0 to -0.7, FCF -0.5 to -0.4
Rule 6 inside-guidance plus rule 9 net-of-segment: the SDA snapback fell from +0.3 to +0.2
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the ABL and secured notes fund maturities to 2028 and are not the negative; the finding was kept on FCF delivery, its sign unchanged
abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged (13.0, 53): the disputed bar pulls p_up toward 50 and the crowded short pulls away, so they offset
